A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RV systolic and dias-tolic function could be impaired in patients affected by cysti-fibrosis without overt cardiovascular disease.
in patients with cystic fibrosis, the right ventricle is affected by a subclinical dysfunction that is not detectable by traditional echocardiographic parameters.
strain echocardiography should be considered for the follow-up of cystic fibrosis patients, especially in those with reduced FEV1 and FEF25– 75% values.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RV 2-D strain is a sensitive marker of RV systolic function in cystic fibrois and it could be a useful tool in the follow up of these patients.
RV strain and TDI are useful to detect subclinical systolic and diastic RV dysfunction in patients with cystic fibrosis.
echocardiography should be performed routinely in cystic fibroses patients, even in the absence of clinical symptoms, in order to detect early subclinical RV dysfunction.
